verdict.line: You lose if you facetank his Granite Shield and trade in his 400-range W/E bubble before level 3; you win if you poke the shield down with Q and punish his commits with E once it's up.

brief.thesis: Malphite's Granite Shield absorbs your first hits every time it's had a breather, so trading into him cold just feeds his passive. Urgot's 800-range Q and 490-range W let you keep chipping that shield from outside his 400-range W (Brutal Strikes) and E (Ground Slam), and E (Disdain) rewards patience, not aggression. The 49.2% head-to-head over 1393 games backs this up as genuinely close, not a losing lane.

theirWindow.what: He eats your opening poke for free and his Brutal Strikes/Ground Slam trade cleanly through it. Don't walk up to melee him when his shield is topped off — he wants that fight.

yourWindow.when: shield cracked, your E is off cooldown
yourWindow.what: Once Q (Corrosive Charge) or autos have burned through Granite Shield, step in behind E (Disdain) — it shields you on the charge and hurls him out of position if it connects, letting you follow with W (Purge) for the Echoing Flames proc.

start.why: Highest-picked start in this matchup (66.8% pick, 49.2% WR over 1148 games) — the sustain and auto damage help you keep poking through Granite Shield without going even on health potions.

boots.why: Best-performing boots here (50.1% WR, 49.3% pick) and relevant since Ground Slam deals magic damage scaling off his armor — the MR cushions that chip damage all lane.

core.why: Top-performing core path (53% WR, 22.2% pick) — the armor shred lets your poke keep punching through his Brutal Strikes-buffed armor window.
Pairs with Black Cleaver in the same build path — the HP and tenacity let you commit to E engages without getting peeled off before you connect.
Third piece of the highest-winrate path (53% over 232 games) — stacking resistances blunts his Ground Slam magic damage and Brutal Strikes armor spike in extended trades.

situational.when: the enemy team is stacking magic damage beyond just malphite (highest-winrate late item at 57% over 86 games)
you're ahead and want to turn your poke lead into sustained teamfight damage (54.5% WR over 101 games)
the enemy has a strong ad crit or burst carry you need to slow down on top of malphite

runes.keystoneWhy: Used in both top rune pages for this matchup; the vulnerable debuff rewards landing consecutive autos while you're poking down Granite Shield from range.
runes.note: This page runs 49.8% WR (16.3% pick) — the better-performing of the two measured pages, and Approach Velocity helps you close the gap faster once your E (Disdain) catches him.

summoners.why: Highest-performing and most-picked combo (49.4% WR, 66.9% pick). Ignite punishes his lack of sustain once you've cracked Granite Shield, since he has no self-heal to fall back on.

playing.title: Poke the shield, not the champion
playing.detail: Granite Shield recharges if Malphite hasn't been hit recently, so land Q (Corrosive Charge) from its 800 range on cooldown to keep it broken rather than letting it refill between trades.

playing.title: Respect his Brutal Strikes window
playing.detail: W (Brutal Strikes) spikes his armor and AD for a short duration on activation — don't initiate a trade the moment you see him turn it on.

playing.title: Stay outside 400 range when not poking
playing.detail: Ground Slam (E, 7s cooldown, 400 range) deals magic damage based on his armor and cuts your attack speed; hovering just outside it denies him easy pokes back.

playing.title: Use E (Disdain) as a punish, not an opener
playing.detail: Wait for him to commit to a melee trade or whiff Q (Seismic Shard, 8s cooldown), then charge E at 475 range to shield yourself and throw him out of position.

playing.title: Sequence W after your other abilities
playing.detail: Purge prioritizes champions you've recently struck with other abilities, so land Q or E first to guarantee it focuses him and triggers Echoing Flames.

playing.title: Back off near his level 6
playing.detail: Unstoppable Force is a long-cooldown (130s at rank 1) dash-knockup — if you're overextended when he hits 6, a flip into Ground Slam and Brutal Strikes can swing a trade hard.

playing.title: Lean on R to zone, not just execute
playing.detail: Fear Beyond Death's 2500 range threat alone can force him off CS once you're ahead on items from the Black Cleaver timing — you don't need to land it every time to get value.

brief.patchCaveat: Build, runes, summoners, and all win rates/sample sizes above are measured from live OP.GG games on the current patch (16.19.1) — the mechanical reasoning and trade patterns are my own read on why those numbers shake out this way.

stats.opponentTip: Do not get hit with (E) by keeping your distance. Get rid of his (P) shield while making sure [E] lands successfully.
